Consider the system of linear equations $Ax = b$ where:
$$A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad b = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}$$
If $(\alpha, \beta, 2)$ is a solution to this system with $\alpha = -5$, find the value of $\beta$.

Consider the subspace $W_1 = \left\{ \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix} \in M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{R}) : a + d = 0 \right\}$ of trace-zero $2 \times 2$ matrices. Consider the matrices:
$$B_1 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, B_2 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}, B_3 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, B_4 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, B_5 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$$
Choose the correct set of matrices that forms a basis for $W_1$:

explanation.value: Trace-zero $2 \times 2$ matrices form a 3-dimensional subspace. $B_2 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$, $B_3 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, and $B_5 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ each have trace 0 and are linearly independent, forming a basis.

prompt.value: Consider the subspace $W_2 = \left\{ \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix} \in M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{R}) : a + b = 0, c + d = 0 \right\}$. Which of the following sets of matrices span $W_2$?

explanation.value: $\dim(W_2) = 2$, and any set that contains a basis for $W_2$ spans $W_2$.

prompt.value:
Suppose $W_1$ and $W_2$ are subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^3$ defined by:
$$W_1 = \{(0, y, z) : y, z \in \mathbb{R}\}, \quad W_2 = \{(x, y, z) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x + y + z = 0\}$$
Which of the following options represents $W_1 \cap W_2$?

explanation.value: Vectors in $W_1 \cap W_2$ satisfy $x = 0$ and $0 + y + z = 0 \implies z = -y$. Thus $W_1 \cap W_2 = \{(0, y, -y)\} = \text{Span}\{(0, 1, -1)\}$. Option A also spans this same 1D line.

prompt.value: Suppose $W_1$ and $W_2$ are subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^3$ defined by $W_1 = \{(0, y, z) : y, z \in \mathbb{R}\}$ and $W_2 = \{(x, y, z) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x + y + z = 0\}$. What is the dimension of $W_1 \cap W_2$?

Suppose $W_1 = \{(0, y, z) : y, z \in \mathbb{R}\}$ and $W_2 = \{(x, y, z) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x + y + z = 0\}$ are subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^3$. Which of the following options is true regarding $W_1 \cup W_2$?

options.value: $W_1 \cup W_2$ is a subspace of dimension 3.
$W_1 \cup W_2$ is a subspace of dimension 2.
$W_1 \cup W_2$ is a subspace of dimension 1.

explanation.value: The union of two subspaces is a subspace if and only if one is contained in the other. Neither $W_1 \subseteq W_2$ nor $W_2 \subseteq W_1$, so $W_1 \cup W_2$ is not a subspace.
